library: Library Borrowing Rules. The university library serves all registered students and staff during term time. Students may borrow up to five books at a time for a period of fourteen days. Borrowed books can be renewed once through the library account unless another reader has reserved them. Reference books, past papers and rare collections must be used inside the reading hall and cannot leave the building under any condition. A fine of twenty rupees is charged for every day a book is returned after the due date, and a student who owes more than five hundred rupees cannot borrow again until the full amount is paid at the accounts office, although a librarian may waive the fine when the student shows a signed medical note that covers the late period and submits it within seven days of returning the book. Lost books must be reported at once, and the student must pay the current price of the book or provide an identical new copy. Silence is required in the reading hall, and food and drinks are not allowed near the shelves. Group study rooms are booked online and may be kept for two hours at a time.
hostel: Hostel Residence Guide. Hostel rooms are allotted at the start of each semester according to the merit list published by the student affairs office. Residents must carry their hostel card at all times and show it to the guard on request. The main gate closes at ten in the evening for every resident. Late entry is allowed only with written permission from the warden, which must be obtained before the gate closes. Visitors may meet residents in the common room between four and seven in the afternoon and are never permitted to enter the bedrooms. Electric heaters, irons and cooking appliances are not allowed inside the rooms because they cause fires and overload the wiring of the building. Residents who wish to leave the hostel permanently must inform the warden one month in advance, return the room key, and clear the room before the inspection, otherwise the security deposit will be deducted. Maintenance requests are written in the complaint register kept at the reception desk.
lab: Computer Lab Usage Policy. The computer labs are open from eight in the morning until six in the evening on weekdays. Students log in with their university account and must log out before leaving the seat. Installing software on lab machines is not allowed, because every computer is restored to its original state each night and any installed program will be removed. Printing is limited to fifty pages per student each week, and extra pages are charged at two rupees per page at the lab counter. Mobile phones must stay silent, and eating or drinking is forbidden near the equipment. Final year students working on a supervised project may request extended access until nine in the evening, but only when their supervisor sends an email to the lab incharge at least two days before the first extra session and names the project and the machines that are needed. Any damaged equipment must be reported to the lab assistant immediately. Saved files should be copied to personal storage because local folders are cleared every night.
contractor: Remote Work Policy. This policy sets out who may work away from the office and who has to approve it. Permanent employees may work from home for up to three days per week once their line manager agrees. Contractors can work remotely only if the signed contract permits it. The employee arrangement does not extend to contractors, which means a line manager cannot give verbal permission to a contractor. If a contract says nothing about remote work, the contractor must keep working on site until human resources amends the contract in writing. An earlier version of this policy, now withdrawn, let contractors work from home for two days a week without any contract clause; any old copy repeating that rule is out of date and must be ignored. To request an amendment, send the contract number to the human resources office, which answers within ten working days. Everyone working remotely must be reachable during office hours, use only company approved laptops, and always connect through the secure network.
printer: Printer Troubleshooting Guide. This guide describes the shared printers on each floor and the faults that users report most often. For blank printer pages, check the ink levels and run the cleaning utility. Afterwards print a test page to confirm the fix and record the outcome in the maintenance log. If the test page is still blank, take out the cartridge, make sure the protective tape is gone and push it back in firmly before trying again. A blank scanner image is a different problem: check how the document is placed and choose the right scanning source rather than following these steps. The old laser machines in the storage room have a drum unit, and for those machines the drum should be replaced when pages come out blank, but that advice is not meant for the current inkjet printers. Do not open a printer while it is working, and switch it off before pulling out a jammed sheet. Report any fault that keeps returning to the help desk, quoting the printer label and the time it failed.
